Committee: Tourism
Sponsor: Jones
Analyst: Julie Knight
Date: 02/09/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 167 as introduced and as amended and reported by the Committee on Tourism allows a winery, an organization of grape growers and certain other entities to obtain a license, in the amount of $150 from the Alcoholic Beverage Control Board, to hold a wine festival, provide tastings, and sell wine for on-premises and off-premises consumption. This bill provides that wine sold at a festival must be taxed in accordance with local, state and federal laws and may not exceed one case of wine per customer per day, which could increase receipts to the Education Trust Fund, State General Fund, the Department of Human Resources, counties and municipalities by an undetermined amount dependent upon the price of the table wine sold by the winery or organization as provided for by law. This bill could also increase receipts to the State General Fund, assuming the license fees are distributed in the same manner as other fees for licenses issued by the board; and would increase the administrative obligations of the Alcoholic Beverage Control Board by an undetermined amount to adopt rules concerning wine festival licensing.
Del Marsh, Chairperson
Tourism

Committee: Boards, Agencies and Commissions
Sponsor: McClendon
Analyst: Bryan Young
Date: 03/26/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 302 as passed the Senate would increase the obligations of the Alabama State Board of Occupational Therapy by an undetermined amount to develop a program to promote early identification, intervention, treatment, and rehabilitation of any impaired licensee and to provide operational expenses, including actual cost of travel, office overhead, and personnel expenses, to members of the Alabama Occupational Therapy Wellness Committee created by this bill.
Howard Sanderford, Chair

Committee: Economic Development and Tourism
Sponsor: Jones
Analyst: Daniel Davenport
Date: 04/13/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 167 as passed the Senate allows a winery, an organization of grape growers and certain other entities to obtain a license, in the amount of $50 from the Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) Board, to hold a wine festival. This bill also allows a retailer or manufacturers to obtain a participant license in the amount of $15 from the ABC Board to provide tastings and sell wine for on-premises and off-premises consumption at a wine festival. This bill provides that wine sold at a festival must be taxed in accordance with local, state and federal laws and may not exceed one case of wine per customer per day, which could increase receipts to the Education Trust Fund, State General Fund, the Department of Human Resources, counties and municipalities by an undetermined amount dependent upon the price of the table wine sold by the winery or organization as provided for by law. This bill could also increase receipts to the State General Fund, assuming the license fees are distributed in the same manner as other fees for licenses issued by the board; and would increase the administrative obligations of the Alcoholic Beverage Control Board by an undetermined amount to adopt rules concerning wine festival licensing.
Becky Nordgren, Chair
Economic Development and Tourism
